description: Two independent generative sequencer lanes, each playing a random pitch sequence at its own tempo with a note envelope, and a Dyn knob that turns steps into long held notes or into rests

params.text: Starts and stops that lane; the lamp is lit while it runs, and stopping it returns the lane to the first step, drops its pitch output to 0V and clears its envelope
Draws sixteen fresh random pitches for that lane, each between 0V and 5V, replacing the sequence in place while the lane carries on playing
Sets how many steps that lane plays before repeating, 2 to 16; the number under the knob is the current setting
Sets that lane's tempo, 1 to 240 BPM, one step per beat; the number under the knob is the current setting

At noon every step fires a short note; turned right a step may instead be held for a whole pass of the sequence, turned left a step may fall silent, and the chance of either is the knob position cubed
Sets the attack time of that lane's note envelope, 0 to 4 seconds; at 0 the envelope jumps straight to 10V
Sets the decay time of that lane's note envelope, 0 to 4 seconds measured from 10V down to 0V

outputs.text: That lane's current pitch, a random value between 0V and 5V held until the next note fires; it is 0V on a dropped step and 0V while the lane is stopped
That lane's note envelope, rising to 10V over the Rise time and falling over the Fall time, and holding at 10V for the length of a held note, despite the panel printing Gate

notes: neither lane produces anything until its Run button is pressed.
there is no clock input and no clock output; each lane is timed by its own BPM knob and the two run independently of each other and of the rest of the patch.
a lane fires a new note only once the previous envelope has finished, so a long Fall time, or a held note, makes the lane pass over steps until the envelope completes.
the pitches are drawn at random between 0V and 5V and are not quantized; patch the 1v/O output through a quantizer for notes in a scale.
